title: The Load-Bearing Hour with Ronnie
description: Ronnie takes home-repair calls on Snazzie FM and answers every one with total confidence and zero competence. Barry tries to flag the danger. The fix for everything is a bookshelf.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM, and it's The Load-Bearing Hour, where your home is falling apart and I tell you it isn't. Lines are open.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, for the record, you have never held a level.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I've held many levels of confidence, Barry. Linda, you're up first. What's the home doing to you tonight?

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: Oh, thank you, Ronnie, I'm so worried. There's this slow brown drip coming through my ceiling, right under the upstairs bathroom, and the stain keeps getting bigger, and... I'm scared the whole floor's gonna come down.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Linda, Linda. Breathe. A brown stain? That's not damage. That's character.

lines.speaker: caller-linda
lines.text: It's character?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Water finds its own level, sweetheart. It'll sort itself out. Get a bigger bucket. <p:0.3> And you know what hides a bucket? A nice bookshelf right under the drip. Guests won't notice a thing.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's a burst pipe, Linda, you should call a...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Bookshelf. Next caller. Gary, talk to me.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: Yeah, hi, Ronnie. There's this smell near my furnace. Kind of a... rotten egg thing? It comes and goes. Is that dangerous?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Rotten eggs? Gary, that's a cooking issue. You're frying too close to the unit.

lines.speaker: caller-gary
lines.text: I don't cook near the furnace, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Then it's a smell looking for a job. Grab a scented plug-in, cover the note, done. Snazzie FM listeners get a discount on Air Prime fresheners, by the way. Lavender masks anything.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Gary, that's gas, you need to evacu...

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And don't light a candle near it, Barry, that's just basic candle safety, everybody knows that. Mildred, you're on.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Hello, dear. My outlet sparks when I plug in the kettle, and it gets warm, and now I'm frightened it'll start a fire in the night.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Warm just means it's working hard, Mildred. That outlet's earning its keep.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: But the sparking, dear?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You don't want an electrician. Trust me. My ex-brother-in-law's an electrician, total snake, charged me for a Tuesday. <p:0.3> Just tape over that outlet and run an extension cord from the good one across the hallway rug. Out of sight, out of mind.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: A cord under a rug is how fires start, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's how rugs get cozy, Barry. Last one. Darnell, bring me your worst.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Okay, so there's a long diagonal crack that just appeared right across my living room wall, and now a door upstairs won't shut, and I'm really worried it's the foundation.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Diagonal crack, door won't shut. Darnell, that's a load-bearing wall. Probably. Who's to say.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Wait, that sounds bad, what do I do?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Knock it out wider. A wall can't crack if there's less of it. Then brace whatever's left with a nice sturdy bookshelf.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I'm done. I'm just... I'm done.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: And congratulations, Darnell. <p:0.3> You've got open concept now.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie. Linda just called back.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Happy customer?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The bookshelf is now upstairs. <p:0.3> Through the floor.
